subject: Day Segment Analysis: Clarification with outputs for Part 2 and Part 5

messages.author: 2f947cbc2c48554d
messages.subject: Day Segment Analysis: Clarification with outputs for Part 2 and Part 5
parts:
Hi all, 

Again, I really appreciate that there is this forum to ask questions about using GGIR to process accelerometer data. 

Regarding activity-log based segmentation, my understanding is that it is implemented in Part 2 and Part 5 as outlined in the main GGIR vignette: 4 Implementation in GGIR. The exceptions are bouted and unbouted behaviour, which only provides a full-day summary, as noted in a previous thread discussion here.  

However, when I use the activity-log to segment my data, I noticed that Part 2 segments  the results according to the activity-log. However, Part 5 outputs a full-day summary. Is this correct or am I missing something? In addition, Part 5 does not provide results for all the days recorded, even though Part 2 does. 

For example, I have one participant with 5 days of recording that I am interested in and have ran the following GGIR code and using qwindow() to read the activity log: 

GGIR(
  #======================
  #GENERAL  
  #======================
  mode = mode,
  datadir = datadir,
  outputdir = outputdir,
  f0 = f0,
  f1 = f1,
  overwrite = TRUE, 
  do.imp = TRUE, 
  idloc = 2,
  print.filename = TRUE, 
  storefolderstructure = FALSE,
  #======================
  # PART 1
  #======================
  windowsizes = c(5, 900, 3600),
  do.cal = TRUE, 
  do.enmo = TRUE, 
  do.anglex = TRUE,
  chunksize = 0.5,
  printsummary = TRUE,
  #=====================
  #PART 2
  #=====================
  data_masking_strategy = 1, 
  hrs.del.start = 0, 
  hrs.del.end = 0, 
  maxdur = 0, 
  includedaycrit = 16, 
  M5L5res = 10, 
  winhr = 5, 
  qlevels = NULL, 
  qwindow = qwindow, 
  qwindow_dateformat = qwindow_dateformat # %d/%m/%Y,
  desiredtz = "Australia/Brisbane",
  ilevels = NULL, 
  mvpathreshold = 100.6, 
  #=====================
  #PART 3  
  #=====================
  timethreshold = 10, 
  anglethreshold = 5,
  ignorenonwear = FALSE,
  #====================
  #PART 4 
  #====================
  includenightcrit = 16,
  def.noc.sleep = 1,
  loglocation = NULL,
  outliers.only = FALSE,
  criterror = 0,
  relyonguider = FALSE,
  do.visual = FALSE,
  #===================
  #PART 5
  #===================
  threshold.lig = 45.8, 
  threshold.mod = 93.2,
  threshold.vig = 418.3, 
  excludefirstlast = FALSE,
  boutcriter = 1, 
  boutcriter.in = 1,
  boutcriter.lig = 1,
  boutcriter.mvpa = 1,
  boutdur.in = c(5, 10, 30, 60), 
  boutdur.lig = c(5, 10, 30, 60),
  boutdur.mvpa = c(5, 10, 30, 60),
  timewindow = c("WW"),
  #=====================
  #REPORT GENERATION
  #=====================
  do.report=c(2, 5),
  visualreport = TRUE,
  dofirstpage = TRUE,
  viewingwindow = 1
) 

part2_daysummar.csv and part2_daysummary_longformat.csv provides results for the five days and segments. However, part5_daysummary only provides full day summaries with only three days of results and part5_personalsummary only one day of results. 

What I was hoping to see in Part 5 was a summary of the minutes in different physical activity levels according to the segments, not full day summaries. Any clarification would be appreciated. 

Attached are the .csv files for Part 2 (day summary), Part 5 (day and person) and the meta .Rdata file. 

Regards,
Kieu

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Day Segment Analysis: Clarification with outputs for Part 2 and Part 5
parts:
Hi Kieu,

Segmenting the day in part 5 only works for timewindow = "MM", it does not work for timewindow "WW" because that window is not aligned with the 24 hour clock.

Part 5 comes with two reports: 
"..._cleaned_..." as stored in results folder, which has the cleaned output without invalid days.
"..._full_..." as stored in the subfolder results/QC and intended to give you the opportunity to understand why certain days were included/excluded.
Note that for part 5 it is especially critical that incomplete days are excluded because they will bias results.

Vincent

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Day Segment Analysis: Clarification with outputs for Part 2 and Part 5
parts: Are you referring to days that have incomplete measurements from midnight to midnight (MM)?

Yes, which can happen on the first or last day of a recording. Here, by default, we expect at least 23 hours of data to be present in a calendar day. The 23 is controlled with parameter minimum_MM_length.part5, so technically you can lower it but I would advise against it. Note that this is about the length of the data regardless of whether sensor was worn. Inclusion of days with sufficient valid data is controlled with parameter includedaycruit.part5.

The reason we made it this stringent is because GGIR does not extrapolate the time series, which then means that if you have less than 24 hours in a day this will disturb the proportional contributions of behaviour to that day. For example, if a recording starts at 11am you may still capture all MVPA during that day but you may fail to capture 3 hours of inactivity that day. As a result, when average this day with the other days in the recording it will bias the average time spent inactivity downward.

Vincent
